subject: NovumHealth private deployment RFI and VPC/air-gap next steps
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
To: Claire Martin <claire.martin@novumhealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-03T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: NovumHealth private deployment RFI and VPC/air-gap next steps

Hi Claire —

Great to speak this morning. Thanks for walking us through NovumHealth’s use case and the high-level constraints around PHI residency and the preferred VPC-only deployment model. To keep momentum, summarized next steps and asks below: 

- Immediate asks for NovumHealth security team (goal: intake this week):
  - Complete the vendor RFI attached (I’ve included a filled starter tab to reduce duplicate questions) — file: novum-security-rfi.xlsx
  - Confirm SOC 2 status (report or letter) and any scoping notes you want us to consider (we can accept a SOC 2 Type II report or an attestation letter)
  - Flag any additional regulatory requirements beyond HIPAA/GDPR (state-specific controls, BAAs)

- From our side:
  - I’ve attached a one-page SOC 2 summary for Redwood and a VPC segmentation template that outlines typical public/private network zones and optional air-gapped staging pools (redwood-soc2-summary.pdf, vpc-segmentation-template.png)
  - @Neha and @Monica will prepare a short deployment sketch showing isolation options and a minimal evidence pack for the items you ask for

Proposed timelines: if you can return the RFI by EOD Thursday we’ll have a preliminary answer set and a high-level architecture sketch by Monday. If that works I’ll schedule a 30-minute follow-up next Tuesday to review the diagram and confirm the compliance checklist.

Attachments: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (stub), vpc-segmentation-template.png (stub), novum-security-rfi.xlsx (starter workbook)

Thanks —
Dylan Brooks
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
D: +1 (415) 555-0192 | dylan@redwood.com
https://www.redwood.com
From: Claire Martin <claire.martin@novumhealth.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Cc: NovumHealth Security Team <security@novumhealth.com>
Date: 2028-05-03T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: NovumHealth private deployment RFI and VPC/air-gap next steps

Thanks Dylan — appreciate the clear summary. A few quick clarifications from our security team: 

- We are SOC 2 Type II in scope for our patient-data services; currently completing the 2027 audit cycle. We can share the most recent bridge letter this week; the full report will be available in Q3.
- HIPAA applicability: NovumHealth will require a BAA; please flag any callouts we should expect in your standard contract.
- Air-gap: we don’t need a full air-gapped production cluster initially, but we will need an isolated staging environment that prevents egress and has strict ingress filters.

I’ve attached our RFI so your team can start filling answers into the workbook. We aim to return a completed vendor checklist for the highest-risk hosts by Thursday.

Attachment: novum-security-rfi.xlsx (Novum internal RFI)

—Claire
Claire Martin
Director, IT Security — NovumHealth
claire.martin@novumhealth.com

FYI — Claire returned the RFI and gave quick scoping guidance (copy below). Can you please: 

1) Start filling the RFI workbook with Redwood answers for sections: SOC 2 scope, data residency, encryption at rest/transport, logging & SIEM integration, BAA support, and typical network controls.
2) Produce a one-page high-level diagram that shows two deployment variants: A) isolated VPC with private NAT + no public endpoints; B) VPC with dedicated public egress and private subnets plus optional air-gap staging (use vpc-segmentation-template.png as base).
3) Assemble a minimal evidence pack (bridge letter, encrypt configs, logging configuration snippets) — place drafts in the shared drive link below.

Timeline: RFI draft by Thursday EOD, diagram Monday morning, internal evidence pack by Monday afternoon. If any of this is unrealistic let me know and propose alternatives.

Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cNovum-RFI

Thanks —
Dylan
